title: The Footnote
logline: Ted's student evaluations come in at a three point one, and the department's top-rated teacher is his pompous former boss Hammond Druthers, now an adjunct his students adore. With the Thesis Studio on the line, Ted goes to war for his students by becoming Hammond, sweater vest and all, while Barney turns Ted's evaluations into an anonymous comments section for the gang that gets personal one lowercase g at a time.
coldOpen: Kids, every professor says they never read their student evaluations. Every professor is lying. In the spring of 2014, I read mine so many times I turned into my old boss.

couch.line: Worse, Luke. A sweater vest thing.

guests.name: Harper Okonkwo
guests.role: a second-year architecture student in both Hammond's class and Ted's; says everything, praise or mockery, in the same flat monotone, calls things 'iconic' without ever explaining which way she means it, and records anything worth recording on her phone

guests.name: Dr. Alastair Fenn
guests.role: chair of the architecture department, a former actuary who announces every number like it's election night, with long dramatic pauses, and finds budget cuts thrilling

scenes.summary: Ted's evaluations arrive: a three point one, while the department's new adjunct, his old boss Hammond Druthers, has a four point nine. A flashback shows how Hammond once credited Ted's work: footnote nineteen, right after the shrimp. The gang reads Ted's comments aloud, and Barney launches an anonymous comments section for the gang. Button: Ted's only five-star review is about Hammond.

beats.line: Every May, my student evaluations arrived in a plain brown envelope.
Guys. My student evaluations. Thirty-one anonymous reviews of Professor Ted Mosby.
Read the comments! I love comments. I read every comment on every casserole recipe on the internet.
He replies. He's been pen pals with a woman in Duluth since 2011. Over a tuna bake.
I don't read them for validation, Lily. I read them to grow.
I lived with him. He reads them in the bathtub. With a highlighter.
Barney. Read me the number. I'm above numbers.
Overall instructor rating. Three point one.
Out of four?
Out of five.
Three point one is fine. Three point one is solid. Respectable. Deeply, deeply average—
Ooh, they rank the whole department!
And in first place, with a four point nine, a brand-new adjunct. Hammond Druthers.
beats.title: Department of Architecture: Spring Evaluations

beats.line: Hammond Druthers? Your old boss? The guy who designed a hospital with no right angles?
The patients got seasick, Marshall. In a building. On land.
Didn't he steal your designs?
He didn't steal them, Lily. He credited me. In a footnote.
Kids, I want to be fair to Hammond. So here's exactly how that footnote happened.
Mosby! The client adores your parking garage. So I've put my name on it.
You promised me credit!
And you have it. Footnote nineteen.
What's footnote eighteen?
The caterer. Her shrimp carried that meeting.
I was credited below shrimp, Lily.
Okay, I'm bored of his feelings. Comments, please.
Comment one. Professor Mosby is very passionate. Mostly about Professor Mosby.
Comment two. I signed up for architecture. I got ninety minutes on the history of the word lintel.
Actually, it was a hundred and five. They're rounding down.
Comment three! Would take again!
Thank you!
If it was the only class left. And I needed the credit. And he stopped saying actually.
Guys. Anonymous feedback. Brutally honest, zero consequences. Why do only professors get this?
Because the rest of us have friends. Who lie to us. Like normal people.
Not anymore. As of tonight, this group has a comments section.
Anonymous? Completely anonymous?
Baby, you just said anonymous the way a cat says bird.
Everyone reviews everyone. Stars and comments. Under my door by Friday.
I'm not reviewing my friends. You're all fives. You're fives forever.
Noted. Marshall Eriksen. Four stars. Too soft.
Ted! Last one. It's five stars!
Read it.
Professor Druthers is a genius. I don't know who Professor Mosby is. Five stars.
That's my only five.

scenes.summary: Ted shows up early to Hammond's class in his own lecture hall. Hammond lectures entirely on Hammond; the students, led by deadpan Harper, call him iconic, and Ted misreads it as confidence. Hammond introduces Ted as footnote nineteen. Department chair Fenn sets the stakes: the higher final evaluation gets the Thesis Studio, with a window; the lower gets Saturday morning drafting. Hammond leads by one point eight. Button: Ted starts his class Hammond-style and Harper picks up her phone.

beats.line: Hammond taught in my lecture hall the hour before me. So I got there fifty-five minutes early.
And this, class, is the Druthers Natatorium. A public swimming pool in the shape of my own signature.
The Times called it unswimmable. Unswimmable! You don't get a word invented for you by accident.
Iconic.
Hammond.
Mosby! Class, this is my former intern. Footnote nineteen.
Professor Mosby. I teach in this room. Right after you.
Ah, yes. The overflow.
So what exactly is this course, Hammond?
Nine weeks of Hammond Druthers. Week ten is a field trip. To look at Hammond Druthers.
We all get on a bus. He stands outside it. We look at him.
Harper? You were in my class last fall.
I wrote the one about lintels.
That was a hundred and five minutes of pure gold.
It was a hundred and ten. I counted.
So what does he have that I don't?
He's like a bald eagle that flies into the same window every week. And never stops believing in himself.
Confidence. They love you because you never doubt yourself.
Doubt is for people with something to doubt, Mosby.
My secret? I never say I think. I only say I know.
I say I think all the time.
I know.
You stand at that lectern like a man apologizing for a building. I have never apologized for a building. Not even the hospital.
Gentlemen! Both of you, in one room. Wonderful. I have numbers.
Budget cuts. Next fall, the department can fund exactly one Thesis Studio.
The Thesis Studio? The one with the window?
The higher final evaluation gets the studio. The lower evaluation teaches...
Saturday morning Intro to Drafting. Seven a.m.
Finals close in two weeks. Current standings. Mr. Druthers leads by...
One point eight.
That's not a lead. That's a landslide.
I know! I haven't been this excited since the copier caught fire.
Two weeks, Hammond. I'm winning my students back.
With what, Mosby? Your little bank?
It's forty stories!
Footnote.
Mosby. The lectern's warm. You're welcome.
Professor Mosby? For what it's worth, your class could be iconic too.
Really?
You'd just have to be a lot more like him.
Class. Today's lecture is about the greatest architect in New York.
Druthers?
Mosby.
Iconic.

scenes.summary: Twelve days later the comments section is in, and it gets personal: Lily IDs Robin's handwriting by her lowercase g, Barney reviewed himself three times, Marshall gave himself a Minnesota four, and Wendy has kept a binder on the booth since 2005. Ted arrives in Hammond's exact vest and tie, calls them footnotes, and boasts a four point six; a flashback shows his 'standing ovation' was students recording a ringtone. The gang gives Ted a three point one too: he's turning into Hammond. Ted exits with Hammond's line.

beats.line: Twelve days. Zero mercy. Ladies, and Marshall, the comments are in.
Marshall Eriksen. Four stars. Talks about Minnesota like it owes him money.
beats.title: Review: Marshall Eriksen
lines: Would hug again. Did. Eleven times.
Talks about Minnesota like it owes him money.

beats.line: Four stars? Who gives a golden retriever four stars?
Robin Scherbatsky. Fun at a bar. Do not ask about feelings, Canada, or the year nineteen ninety-three.
Fair. Accurate. Rude.
Lily Aldrin. Two stars. Would not tell her a secret. Would not tell her a secret about a secret.
Who wrote that?
It's anonymous.
Barney, I teach kindergarten. I can identify any child in Manhattan by their lowercase g.
And this g has a little tail. Like it's running away from a commitment.
Fine. You told Marshall about my root canal before I'd left the dentist.
You were in pain, Robin! Marshall had a right to know!
I sent soup.
And Barney Stinson. Five stars. Five stars. Five stars.
Those are all in your handwriting.
Great minds.
And one star. Nobody knows what this course is about.
Please.
Then who gave you four stars? That four is closed at the top. That's a Minnesota four.
It was me.
Lilypad, in Minnesota, five stars is bragging. Four stars is how we say, I'm doing great.
Oh, you guys do comments now? I've been keeping comments on this booth since 2005.
What do we get?
It's a binder.
Ted. Is that a sweater vest?
It's a waistcoat of conviction.
Footnotes. Gather round.
Did you just call us footnotes?
Affectionately. It's what great men call the people standing near them.
Twelve days ago, I was a three point one. Today's midterm check-in?
Four point six.
Ted! That's amazing!
I don't say I think anymore. I say I know. I rewrote the syllabus. Week one, Mosby. Week two, Mosby, continued.
My students adore the new me. Yesterday I got a standing ovation.
Kids, in the interest of accuracy, here's that standing ovation.
A Mosby is not a building. A Mosby is a feeling.
Iconic. Can you say it again? Slower?
A Mosby is a feeling.
Now angrier. For the people in the back.
A Mosby is a feeling!
Ted. They're recording you.
Because it's quotable.
Because it's a ringtone.
Dad. Half my school still has that ringtone.
I know, Penny. It went off four times during your eighth-grade graduation.
Speaking of reviews. Ted, we reviewed you too.
Let me guess. Four point nine.
Three point one.
That's exactly what my students gave me!
Ted, we've been taking your class for nine years.
And there's one comment we all wrote. Separately. In four different g's.
Professor Mosby is turning into the guy he complained about for nine years.
I am nothing like Hammond Druthers.
Ted, that's his exact tie.
His is blue. Mine is navy. Totally different.
You bought it from him, Ted. For forty dollars.
He was clearing out his closet. Great men travel light.
Footnotes. The booth is warm. You're welcome.
That's going in the binder.

scenes.summary: The adjunct office, final evaluations. Ted wins the Thesis Studio by a tenth of a point, and Fenn cheerfully tells Hammond his contract is over. Hammond's firm closed two years ago. Ted tries to tell him his students adore him; Hammond knows they're laughing. He does it because they come back. Ted sees himself, gives Hammond the studio and takes Saturday drafting. Hammond puts the moment in his memoir, as a footnote. The gang arrives: Marshall upgrades Ted to a Minnesota four, Barney out-self-reviews Hammond, Lily keeps confessing. Future Ted: footnote nineteen.

beats.line: Professor Mosby! Just in time. I've been up since four.
Hammond, they put you by the copier?
Adjuncts don't get windows, Mosby. I look at the copier and I imagine Paris.
Gentlemen. Final evaluations. Hammond Druthers.
Four point six.
Ted Mosby.
Four point seven.
Four point seven! Who's the footnote now?
Congratulations, Professor. The Thesis Studio is yours. Window and all.
Mr. Druthers, with no studio, your contract ends in May. Kyle will need your stapler by Friday.
Wait. Your contract ends?
Mosby, please. A Druthers doesn't need a contract. A Druthers needs a canvas.
So you'll go back to the firm.
The firm closed two years ago. The associates left first. Then the Druthers.
That's why you sold me the tie.
Wear it well. That tie once met the mayor of Hoboken.
Do you know what an architect is without a building, Mosby? A man at a bus stop with opinions.
Hammond, you'll land somewhere. Your students adore you.
Mosby. They're laughing at me.
You know?
I'm pompous, Mosby. I'm not deaf.
Then why keep doing the bit?
Because they come back. Every Tuesday. Thirty-one of them.
Thirty years, Mosby. Nobody ever came back to a Druthers building on purpose.
That's why I talk about lintels for a hundred and five minutes. I'm just hoping somebody stays after.
That's all architecture is, Mosby. You build a room and hope someone stays in it.
I bought this vest to become you. Turns out I didn't need it.
No, you needed the vest. It's doing a lot for you.
Dr. Fenn!
I'd like to give the Thesis Studio to Professor Druthers.
And you'd take Saturday morning drafting? Seven a.m.?
Somebody has to tell those kids about lintels.
This is the most exciting thing to happen here since the copier fire! Mr. Druthers, the window is yours.
Mosby. I don't know what to say.
That has never happened. It's going in the memoir.
Am I in your memoir?
Footnote.
Ted! We're here to take the four point seven out for a drink!
I gave it away. Hammond gets the studio. I get Saturdays at seven.
Ted. I'm revising your review.
Five stars?
Four. A Minnesota four.
Your friends review each other? Then put me down. Five stars, Hammond Druthers. Signed, Hammond Druthers.
Rookie. I reviewed myself three times.
Robin, I'm sorry I told Marshall about your root canal. And your mom's voicemail. And the hockey player.
You told Marshall about the hockey player?
Two stars. I know.
Kids, Hammond taught that Thesis Studio for six more years. Every Tuesday they laughed. And every Tuesday, they came back.
In his memoir, I'm footnote nineteen, after the shrimp. It says, my finest student. I never took his class.
